nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_exists

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_functional

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_zero_prefix

nodes.name: polynomial_zero_extended_shift_forward

nodes.name: polynomial_zero_extended_shift_reverse

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_term_shift_right_iff

nodes.name: prime_field_convolution_coefficient_shift_right_iff

nodes.name: polynomial_product_length_shift_right_nonempty

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_shift_right_nonempty

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_shift_right_empty

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_shift_right_equivalent

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_shift_right_exists

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_power_zero

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_power_successor
nodes.summary: Each actual coefficient at power k becomes the same coefficient at power S k; together with constant zero this is genuine multiplication by X, not evaluation equality.

nodes.name: beta_sum_pointwise_mod_scale

nodes.name: polynomial_zero_extended_scale_congruent

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_term_right_scale_congruent

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_sum_right_scale_congruent

nodes.name: prime_field_convolution_coefficient_right_scale
nodes.summary: At every natural index the actual scaled-input convolution coefficient is the actual canonical product of k and the original coefficient, including all exterior coefficients and composite moduli.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_scale
nodes.summary: Scaling the actual right input preserves the proper representation length and gives the actual scalar action on the product output, including empty factors and zero scalars.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_scale_equal
nodes.summary: Every actual product A*(k B) agrees coefficientwise with every actual scalar result k*(A*B), at the same proper length; no equality of beta codes follows.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_scale_exists
nodes.summary: At any nonzero modulus and canonical scalar, construct the actual scaled input, its actual convolution, and an independently encoded scalar output, then derive their exact decoded-prefix agreement.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_scale_zero_value
nodes.summary: Every actual scalar-zero output is an actually all-zero prefix, without primality and without dropping the scalar bound on an empty input.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_scale_zero
nodes.summary: An actual product with a scalar-zero right input has a genuine zero output prefix at its actual proper length, including empty factors and composite nonzero moduli.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_append_shift_constant_add
nodes.summary: Every actual appended prefix is the actual aligned sum of a genuine trailing-zero shift and the leading-padded singleton constant; the last and earlier entries are proved separately, including M=0.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_append_shift_constant_decomposition_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the shifted old prefix, a canonical singleton constant and its genuine leading padding, then prove their actual aligned sum is the given appended prefix.

nodes.name: prime_field_convolution_coefficient_right_append_add
nodes.summary: At every natural coefficient index, an actual right append is the actual field sum of the old convolution coefficient and the product with the padded singleton constant, using genuine diagonal sums and residues rather than a finite-evaluation identity.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_scale_aligned_sum_exists
nodes.summary: Construct actual shift and scalar outputs, harmless leading paddings to the common length L+S N, and their actual coefficient sum; the commuted S N+L bound is explicitly reconciled, including both empty inputs.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_append_equivalent
nodes.summary: An actual right-factor append satisfies A*append(C,c) formally equivalent to X*(A*C)+c*A through genuine products and arbitrary actual aligned sum outputs. Lengths are not falsely equated in empty cases, and no finite-field evaluation agreement replaces all formal coefficients.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_right_append_exists
nodes.summary: From an actual old product and a canonical next coefficient, construct the appended right factor, its proper product, the shift and scalar outputs, both aligned paddings and the actual sum, then prove the formal recurrence. No output existence or polynomial identity is assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_equivalent_congruent
nodes.summary: Two actual trailing-zero shifts preserve formal coefficient equivalence across arbitrary represented lengths, including empty prefixes. The proof obtains actual predecessor-power coefficients and compares decoded values, without any modulus, primality, coefficient-bound, raw-code identity, or evaluation-equality assumption.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_shift_scale_aligned_equivalent
nodes.summary: For actual AB and AQ, multiplying an actual leading-pad-aligned sum XQ+cB by A is formally equivalent to every actual aligned sum X(AQ)+c(AB). All four intermediate products are genuinely constructed, scalar and shift outputs remain actual graph witnesses, proper product lengths are independent, and no associativity hypothesis or output equality is assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_shift_scale_aligned_congruent
nodes.summary: Formal equivalence of two old prefixes preserves every actual aligned sum of their trailing-zero shifts with a fixed actual scalar multiple of the same source. Both old lengths, all shift/scale encodings, both leading paddings and the sum encodings remain independent; only formal output coefficients are concluded equal.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_associativity_append_step
nodes.summary: An actual formal-coefficient associativity hypothesis for one rightmost prefix extends through one genuine appended coefficient. Every old and new product is an actual proper-length convolution; the proof derives the canonical appended coefficient bound, constructs three real shift/scale/pad/add alignments and a real intermediate product, and concludes only the next formal equivalence. Empty factors are retained, no successor product-length identity is assumed, and the induction step alone is not full associativity.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_nested_empty_right_equivalent
nodes.summary: At every nonzero modulus, actual Q=B*empty, R=P*empty and S=A*Q have formally equivalent all-zero outputs, for arbitrary actual P. The argument constructs the genuine empty zero-prefix fact and transports it through the real products; it assumes neither P=AB nor an output-length shortcut.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_associative_equivalent
nodes.summary: Draft universal rightmost-length induction for formal equivalence of actual (A*B)*C and A*(B*C). The induction predicate quantifies all rightmost codes and proper-length output triples, the successor genuinely constructs three prefix products and decodes the actual endpoint, and the empty base retains arbitrary encodings. This statement is not a successful proof observation until its original body and its exact step dependency are genuinely checked.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_from_product

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_divisor_bounded
nodes.summary: The actual witnessed convolution supplies a canonical divisor prefix, including zero-length divisors.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_dividend_bounded
nodes.summary: Right-factor divisibility is a relation on canonical target prefixes, not on arbitrary unbounded coefficient encodings.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_equivalent_target
nodes.summary: Changing the canonical target by all-power formal coefficient equivalence preserves the same genuine quotient/product witnesses, independently of representation length.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_empty
nodes.summary: Every canonical divisor divides every encoding of the empty polynomial, using an actual empty quotient and actual empty product. No prime, nonzero modulus or nonempty divisor assumption is needed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_equivalent_divisor
nodes.summary: An equivalent canonical right divisor preserves divisibility by constructing the quotient times the replacement at its own actual proper length. Formal output congruence, not a supplied output identity, gives the new witness.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_transitive
nodes.summary: Actual Q1*D equivalent to A and Q2*A equivalent to B give the actual composite quotient Q2*Q1. Three genuine intermediate products, formal associativity and right-input congruence prove its product with D equivalent to B. No commutativity, fixed representation lengths or raw-code identities are assumed.

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_left_unit_first_term
nodes.summary: The first actual antidiagonal term of a length-one left unit is the chosen right-input coefficient, without any primality or commutativity assumption.

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_left_unit_tail_term
nodes.summary: Every later term is zero because its left input index is outside a genuine length-one prefix. The value of that prefix is irrelevant here.

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_left_unit_natural_sum
nodes.summary: An actual unit-left antidiagonal sum equals its first coefficient: construct the one-term sum and use the proved zero-tail invariant on all remaining actual summands.

nodes.name: prime_field_convolution_coefficient_left_unit
nodes.summary: The actual residue of the unit-left natural sum is its already bounded right-input value. No polynomial equality is hidden among the premises.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_left_unit_equal
nodes.summary: Every coefficient of an actual length-L product U*A agrees with A when U is a length-one unit, including the vacuous L=0 case.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_left_unit_equivalent
nodes.summary: Actual left multiplication by a length-one unit preserves formal coefficients, not just evaluations or a selected encoding.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_convolution_left_unit_exists
nodes.summary: Construct an actual canonical length-one unit and its actual length-L left product, formally equal to A. The proper length is zero when A is empty.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_reflexive
nodes.summary: Every canonical polynomial right-divides itself using a constructed left unit and actual product. Empty and zero prefixes are included, without assuming commutative multiplication.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bounded_representative_at_length_exists
nodes.summary: From L<=K construct a genuine leading-zero beta prefix of length K, retain canonical coefficients, and prove formal equivalence to the input, including empty prefixes.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_same_length

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_transport
nodes.summary: Independent formal recodings of the original inputs preserve the same actual common representatives, without asserting a padding length inequality.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_at_length_exists
nodes.summary: Construct two actual canonical common-length representatives by independent leading-zero padding at any supplied common upper bound.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_exists
nodes.summary: Use the explicit common length L+M to construct real canonical representatives for any two independently sized inputs, including zero lengths.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_functional

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_representatives_symmetric
nodes.summary: Swapping the two original inputs and their actual representatives preserves the common-representation graph.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_from_common
nodes.summary: Package actual common representatives, an actual coefficient sum, and formal output equivalence while retaining all three original canonical coefficient guards.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_bounded
nodes.summary: Aligned addition includes canonical coefficients for the actual originals and output, not merely for equivalent witnesses.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_from_fixed
nodes.summary: Every genuine fixed-length addition supplies its own actual common representatives and is an aligned addition, without an extra prime hypothesis.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_transport
nodes.summary: Independent formal recoding of all three canonical originals preserves a real aligned sum; canonicality is never inferred solely from equivalence.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_commutative
nodes.summary: Actual aligned addition commutes by swapping its real common representatives and the checked coefficient addition.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_functional
nodes.summary: Two actual aligned sums represent the same formal polynomial even when their witnesses, original output lengths, and beta codes differ.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_exists
nodes.summary: Construct a genuine canonical aligned sum at the explicit length L+M from any two canonical inputs, rather than assuming operation witnesses.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_realize

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_subtract_from_fixed

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_subtract_exists
nodes.summary: Construct actual aligned field subtraction at length L+M, using real canonical common representatives and the genuine solution B+R=A.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_cancel_left
nodes.summary: Cancel a common addend from actual aligned sums: construct four real common-length prefixes, realize both additions and apply checked coefficient subtraction functionality.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_associative
nodes.summary: Both actual bracketings of three independently sized polynomials give formally equivalent outputs; all seven comparison prefixes and all four coefficient operations are genuinely constructed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_subtract_functional
nodes.summary: Actual aligned subtraction has a formally unique result, including unequal lengths and unrelated beta encodings.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_add_trim_aligned
nodes.summary: An actual fixed-length sum and actual trim supply real common representatives for the canonical product and trimmed remainder; no prime premise or equality of unused beta entries is needed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_execution_aligned_identity

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_convolution_left_add
nodes.summary: Actual left products distribute over an independently represented aligned sum: construct real equal-length products of its witnesses and prove formal equivalence to the three supplied outputs, including empty-factor cases.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_convolution_right_add
nodes.summary: Actual right products distribute over an independently represented aligned sum: construct real equal-length products of its witnesses and prove formal equivalence to the three supplied outputs, including empty-factor cases.

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_left_constant_first_term
nodes.summary: The first actual antidiagonal term of a genuine left singleton is the ordered natural product k*a. No modulus, coefficient bound, or commutativity premise is needed.

nodes.name: polynomial_diagonal_left_constant_natural_sum
nodes.summary: The actual finite natural sum equals k*a: construct its one-term sum and use the existing zero-tail invariant for every subsequent summand. The total need not itself be a canonical field coefficient.

nodes.name: prime_field_convolution_coefficient_left_constant
nodes.summary: Every actual in-range constant-left convolution coefficient is the canonical residue of the ordered product k*a. Both input bounds and the actual natural-sum witness are explicit; primality is unnecessary for this implication.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_left_constant_product_to_scale
nodes.summary: An actual length-L product of a canonical left singleton and a length-L prefix yields the existing scalar graph, even when L=0. The scalar bound follows from the singleton rather than from vacuous output entries.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_scale_to_left_constant_product
nodes.summary: Recover the genuine LEFT-constant convolution on the supplied scalar-output codes. Every needed antidiagonal sum is actually constructed and its residue identified; the empty proper-length branch is separate, including scalar zero and characteristic two.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_left_constant_product_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the canonical singleton and actual scalar output, then prove their genuine left-factor product using those same output codes. Empty source prefixes still require a canonical scalar and singleton; no beta-code uniqueness or gcd endpoint is claimed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_remainder_length_descent
nodes.summary: Every actual normalized remainder has retained length at most d and strictly less than the actual divisor length S d. The zero branch is handled directly; the nonzero branch uses its genuine represented-degree length equation.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_constant_remainder_empty
nodes.summary: Actual division by the nonzero degree-zero divisor produces an empty normalized remainder, including an empty dividend. This assigns no degree to the zero polynomial.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_scale_implies_right_divides
nodes.summary: A genuine scalar output is a right multiple of its source: construct an actual LEFT singleton quotient and actual product, then transport the independently encoded product to the supplied target by decoded-prefix equality. Empty inputs and scalar zero are included.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_monic_normalization_right_associates
nodes.summary: An actual monic normalization and its genuinely inverted scalar action supply actual right-divisibility witnesses in both directions. These witnesses use left constant quotients; no polynomial commutativity, unit-associate oracle, or equality of beta codes is used.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_normalized_right_associate_exists
nodes.summary: Construct a zero-or-monic right associate of every canonical polynomial, first trimming its actual leading zeros and then normalizing only a nonempty trim. Both divisibility directions have real product witnesses and are transported to the original representation. Empty and all-zero encodings need no degree or inverse of zero.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_aligned_add
nodes.summary: A common actual right divisor divides the genuine aligned add: construct the corresponding quotient operation and its proper product, use checked right distributivity and compare real aligned sums.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_aligned_subtract
nodes.summary: A common actual right divisor divides the genuine aligned subtract: construct the corresponding quotient operation and its proper product, use checked right distributivity and compare real aligned sums.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_left_product
nodes.summary: An actual right divisor of B divides every actual left multiple Q*B; the composed quotient is supplied by the checked constructive transitivity theorem.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_common_right_divisor_euclidean_transport
nodes.summary: A genuine Euclidean identity A=Q*B+R preserves precisely the actual common right divisors in both directions, using constructed quotient sums and differences.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_execution_common_right_divisors
nodes.summary: Every genuine polynomial division execution preserves common right divisors, including the empty quotient and zero remainder, with its aligned identity constructed from the execution.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_euclidean_backward_coefficient_identity
nodes.summary: From genuine products and the actual difference T=U-V*Q, prove G=V*A+T*B by ordered distributivity, actual convolution associativity and aligned addition reassociation; the desired sum is a conclusion.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bezout_euclidean_backward
nodes.summary: Construct W=V*Q, T=U-W, and genuine new products to turn an actual Bezout representation for (B,R) into one for (A,B), with both coefficient-update graphs returned as witnesses.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_execution_bezout_backward
nodes.summary: A real division execution automatically supplies the proper Euclidean identity and constructs the exact backward Bezout coefficient update, including an empty quotient.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_aligned_add_empty_right
nodes.summary: Construct a real zero prefix at the input length and its formal equivalence to the empty polynomial, giving an actual aligned right-zero sum for every canonical input.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bezout_from_right_multiple
nodes.summary: An actual right multiple G of A supplies its real left quotient U. With the empty coefficient V, construct V*B and an actual aligned sum to give G=U*A+V*B. The second input only needs canonical coefficients.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bezout_equivalent_transport
nodes.summary: Independently recode both inputs and the result by formal coefficient equivalence, retaining the same Bezout coefficients. Construct both new proper products; output equivalences are proved, not supplied as premises. No primality is needed beyond a nonzero modulus.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bezout_common_right_divisor
nodes.summary: Every actual common right divisor of A and B divides any actual Bezout representative G=U*A+V*B. This is the greatestness implication, not an assertion that an arbitrary Bezout representative divides either input.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_division_remainder_bounded
nodes.summary: The actual trim inside division supplies canonical remainder coefficients, including its empty branch; no primality or degree of zero is assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_reduced_representative_exists
nodes.summary: Construct a formally equivalent canonical representative of no greater retained length, either empty or with an actual nonzero leading coefficient and represented degree. This trims stored leading zeros without requiring a prime modulus.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_gcd_bezout_empty_second
nodes.summary: Construct an already zero-or-monic common divisor and actual Bezout coefficients for (A,empty), using genuine mutual right-associate witnesses. Empty and all-zero A, including (0,0), require no inverse or degree of zero.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_gcd_bezout_equivalent_second
nodes.summary: Replace the second input by any formally equivalent canonical representation while keeping the same zero-or-monic common divisor and the same Bezout coefficients; both new products remain witnessed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_gcd_bezout_division_backward
nodes.summary: Carry an already normalized common divisor through an actual Euclidean step. Construct the new coefficients V and U-V*Q from actual products and aligned subtraction, preserving the same G.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_gcd_bezout_exists_up_to
nodes.summary: Ordinary natural induction constructs actual normalized gcd and Bezout witnesses for every pair with second retained length at most n. Both input triples are generalized, a stored zero divisor is trimmed before division, and every genuine recursive call has a proved smaller bound.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_gcd_bezout_exists
nodes.summary: Take the actual second representation length as induction bound. No supplied quotient, gcd, degree, termination certificate, or Bezout coefficients are premises.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_bezout_is_right_gcd
nodes.summary: A common right divisor with an actual Bezout representation satisfies the full universally quantified greatestness property, including a zero gcd; no normalization assumption is needed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_normalized_gcd_bezout_exists
nodes.summary: Every pair of canonical polynomials over a prime field has an actual zero-or-monic greatest common right divisor and actual Bezout coefficients. The normalized-gcd definition and the existing Bezout graph occur literally in the conclusion.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_nonzero_leading_equivalent_length_bound
nodes.summary: A nonzero coefficient at the leading power cannot be matched by an outside-prefix zero. This length bound needs neither primality nor canonical coefficients.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_equivalent_represented_degrees_equal
nodes.summary: Formal equivalence preserves genuine represented degree across independently encoded and independently length-annotated nonzero-leading prefixes.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_product_equivalent_nonzero_left_nonempty
nodes.summary: An actual product formally equal to a nonzero-leading representation cannot have an empty left factor. No degree is assigned to empty factors.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_represented_factorization
nodes.summary: Trim the actual quotient, construct an independent proper-length product, and transport formal coefficients. Its genuine nonzero degree e satisfies e+d=a; no quotient degree or domain cancellation is assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_right_divides_represented_degree_bound
nodes.summary: A nonzero represented right divisor has degree at most that of its nonzero represented multiple, using the actual retained quotient degree as the natural witness.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_monic_singleton_multiple_equivalent
nodes.summary: Both monic heads force an actual left singleton quotient to have coefficient one, by the ordered leading product k*1. The genuine left-unit convolution law then gives formal equivalence.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_monic_equal_degree_right_divides_equivalent
nodes.summary: Equal-degree monic right divisibility has a genuinely constructed degree-zero quotient. Its head must be one, so divisor and target are formally equivalent.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_monic_right_associates_equivalent
nodes.summary: Mutual right divisibility forces equal represented degrees. Both actual monic normalizations then force formal coefficient equivalence, without selecting unique beta codes.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_empty_right_divisor_implies_equivalent_zero
nodes.summary: An empty right divisor has only formally zero multiples, at any target representation length. The actual product length is zero; no zero-degree assertion or prime hypothesis is used.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_normal_right_associates_equivalent
nodes.summary: Two zero-or-monic mutual right associates are formally equivalent, including both-zero and one-empty branches. Both normalization premises are essential; beta encodings need not agree.

nodes.name: prime_field_polynomial_normalized_gcd_equivalent_unique
nodes.summary: The grouped normal/common-divisor/greatestness graph yields mutual right associates, hence uniqueness only up to formal coefficient equivalence. This does not assert unique beta codes or Bezout coefficients.

nodes.summary: p is nonunit and every factorization of p has a unit factor.

nodes.summary: x is the bounded beta-decoded value at index i.

nodes.name: CanonicalModularResidue
nodes.summary: A strictly bounded canonical natural residue r<m together with exact balanced congruence to a modulo m.

nodes.name: FpAdd
nodes.summary: Bounded operands and the actual canonical residue of their natural sum. The old ND0023 residue graph is reused exactly.

nodes.name: FpMul
nodes.summary: Bounded operands and the actual canonical residue of their natural product; no multiplication law is assumed.

nodes.name: BetaPrefixInto
nodes.summary: Every actual beta entry below the strict length l has a witnessed value below B. The same generic graph describes canonical polynomial coefficients when B is the modulus; empty prefixes are allowed.

nodes.name: BetaPrefixEqual
nodes.summary: Every decoded source entry at i<l also decodes in the target. Actual beta totality and functionality make this extensional prefix equality, not equality of the two code parameters.

nodes.name: FpPolyAdd
nodes.summary: Witnessed canonical addition at each aligned coefficient position. Coefficients are highest-degree-first, and l is a common representation length, not a claimed degree.

nodes.name: FpPolyScale
nodes.summary: A scalar k

nodes.name: BetaZeroExtend
nodes.summary: Decode the genuine beta entry when i<L and return zero when L<=i. This explicitly length-annotated zero extension imposes no false condition on raw beta values beyond the represented prefix.

nodes.name: PolynomialDiagonalTerm
nodes.summary: Witness k with j+k=i and multiply the two actual zero-extended coefficients. These are natural products in a highest-degree-first antidiagonal, before reduction modulo the field prime.

nodes.name: PolynomialDiagonalPrefix
nodes.summary: A real beta table contains the actual antidiagonal products for j<l. The full window l=S i is constructed, so every complementary index is natural.

nodes.name: FpConvolutionCoefficient
nodes.summary: Build the S i antidiagonal terms, take their actual natural Sum, then take its canonical residue r modulo p. No evaluation-product identity or degree assertion is assumed.

nodes.name: PolynomialProductLength
nodes.summary: The proper product representation is empty if either input is empty; otherwise L+M=S N. This is a representation-length relation, not a claim that a possibly zero-leading polynomial has that degree.

nodes.name: FpConvolutionPrefix
nodes.summary: Every output coefficient at i<l is the independently defined actual antidiagonal sum residue. The finite output beta table is constructed rather than postulated.

nodes.name: FpPolyProduct
nodes.summary: Canonical input prefixes, the proper product length, and a genuine convolution output prefix. Terms beyond this length vanish by a separate support theorem, not by assuming the discarded tail is zero.

nodes.name: FpRepresentedDegree
nodes.summary: A length-annotated canonical coefficient prefix has L=S d and an actually decoded nonzero leading coefficient. This does not assign degree to zero or normalize arbitrary leading-zero representations.

nodes.name: FpCoefficientSubtraction
nodes.summary: At each aligned i<L, actual source entries a,b and result entry r satisfy FpAdd(p,b,r,a). All values are the inherited canonical natural field representatives. The graph assumes no subtraction identity, output construction, degree or equality of raw beta codes. Empty prefixes remain vacuous at every modulus.

nodes.name: PolynomialSuffix
nodes.summary: For every i<M and actual source value at t+i, the target beta prefix records that same value at i. No coefficient bound, primality, total input length, zero-prefix condition or suffix construction is assumed. The affine-slice construction theorem is not itself a definition-expansion edge.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialTrim
nodes.summary: The actual input has canonical coefficients and length L=t+M, its first t coefficients are zero, and an actual suffix code has length M. The suffix is empty or its decoded head is nonzero. Primality, a claimed degree, length uniqueness and an output-code uniqueness law are not definition clauses.

nodes.name: FpMonic
nodes.summary: A nonempty canonical coefficient prefix has actual leading coefficient natural 1. Its length is still a representation annotation, not a degree definition; the empty zero polynomial is excluded. Natural field one is not signed code 2, and primality is not included in this graph.

nodes.name: FpInv
nodes.summary: An explicitly nonzero input and an actual product equal to canonical one. This relation never declares zero invertible.

nodes.name: FpMonicNormalization
nodes.summary: For nonempty length L, k is an actual inherited field inverse of the decoded source leading coefficient, and the result is its actual coefficientwise FpPolyScale action. Result monicity, degree preservation and represented-value uniqueness are separate conclusions, not premises. A recorded inverse can also exist at a composite modulus.

nodes.name: PolynomialLeftPad
nodes.summary: The target has t actual leading zero entries and then copies the L decoded source entries. It has annotated length t+L. This is left padding in highest-degree-first order, not right padding or multiplication by X. Canonical coefficients, a field modulus and formal polynomial equality are not assumptions of this graph.

nodes.name: PolynomialPowerCoefficient
nodes.summary: The actual coefficient of X^k is decoded at the index i with i+S k=L, or is zero when L<=k. Empty representations therefore have every formal coefficient zero. This is a coefficient of a formal polynomial, not its value at a field element.

nodes.name: PolynomialEquivalent
nodes.summary: At every natural power, every actual decoded coefficient of the two length-annotated polynomials agrees. Different representation lengths and beta encodings are allowed. This does not identify polynomials merely because their evaluations agree over a finite field; coefficient existence and equivalence laws are separate theorems.

nodes.name: PolynomialQuotientLength
nodes.summary: The representation length q is zero with L<=d, or q is nonzero with q+d=L. Here the divisor has length S d. This specifies max(L-d,0) without a subtraction function and says nothing about the resulting polynomial degree or a quotient identity.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialQuotientStep
nodes.summary: Read the actual input coefficient a, compute the convolution coefficient c using only the already-built length-i quotient prefix, choose the actual field difference s with c+s=a, and record q=k*s. The supplied k need not yet be an inverse. Correctness of the resulting coefficient cancellation is a proved consequence, not a clause of this execution step.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialQuotientPrefix
nodes.summary: Each actual quotient entry at i<N satisfies the genuine triangular execution step using only its earlier quotient prefix. The empty execution is meaningful for every encoding and modulus. Construction, canonical bounds, functionality and coefficient recovery are not graph premises.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialDivisionExecution
nodes.summary: Canonical input coefficients, the quotient representation length, an actual inverse of the decoded divisor head, and an actual quotient execution are recorded. An ambient length-L convolution prefix P is constructed, the actual aligned difference A-P is formed, and its leading zeros are trimmed to the remainder. Neither A=Q*B+R nor a remainder-degree bound is assumed; both require separate proof. Primality is an existence hypothesis, not a definition clause. Empty quotients and empty remainders are retained.

nodes.name: PolynomialShift
nodes.summary: Copy the actual length-L decoded prefix and append a genuine zero at index L. The target length is S L. This is multiplication by X, not harmless leading-zero padding. Primality, canonical bounds, covariance and formal equivalence are not clauses of this graph. Raw beta codes and later entries remain unrestricted.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialRightDivides
nodes.summary: The target A is canonical and there are actual quotient and product triples Q,P such that Q*D=P and P is formally coefficient-equivalent to A. D is the right factor. Product lengths and beta encodings are independent; field evaluations or raw code equality do not replace formal equivalence. Primality, gcd existence and Bezout witnesses are not definition clauses.

nodes.name: CommonRepresentatives
nodes.summary: A_L is formally coefficient-equivalent to U_K and B_M to V_K. The two equivalences form one literal grouped conjunction. No coefficient bound, prime modulus, upper bound on the original lengths, existence witness, raw-code equality or field-evaluation equality is a clause. Legitimate shorter representatives and independent beta encodings are allowed.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialAlignedAdd
nodes.summary: All three originals A_L, B_M and R_N have canonical coefficients. There exist actual common-length representatives U_K,V_K and a true coefficient sum T_K, with CommonRepresentatives(A,B,U,V,K), FpPolyAdd(U,V,T,K), and formal coefficient equivalence T_K~R_N. Primality, existence, uniqueness and algebraic laws are separate theorem statements, not definition clauses.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialAlignedSubtract
nodes.summary: The literal argument permutation FpPolynomialAlignedAdd(p,B_M,R_N,A_L): B+R=A with all three original coefficient guards and actual sum witnesses. This is not an additional subtraction oracle or a proved subtraction law.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialCommonRightDivisor
nodes.summary: D is an actual right divisor of both canonical targets A and B, using two independent quotient/product witness sets. The two RightDivides clauses form one literal conjunction. Existence of a common divisor, greatestness, primality and a gcd theorem are not definition clauses.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialBezoutRepresentation
nodes.summary: There are actual proper products U*A=P and V*B=Q, and an actual aligned sum P+Q=G. Codes and all five original representation lengths remain independent. This is representation data, not a Bezout-existence theorem, a gcd or greatestness result, evaluation equality, or equality of raw codes.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialZeroOrMonic
nodes.summary: The representation is empty or is an actual nonempty canonical monic prefix. No primality or existence claim is included; empty codes are unrestricted.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialRightGcd
nodes.summary: G is a common right divisor, and every common right divisor D right-divides G. This universally quantified property does not assert existence or uniqueness.

nodes.name: FpPolynomialNormalizedGcd
nodes.summary: Literal conjunction of zero-or-monic and right-gcd; no Bezout coefficients or polynomial algorithm are built into this property.
